topic: James Watt Condenser and Thermodynamic Expansion Engine

claims.statement: The separate condenser isolates cyclic cooling from the main cylinder, preventing repetitive thermal quenching of the cylinder walls.
claims.verifiableSource: Dickinson HW. (A Short History of the Steam Engine, Cambridge University Press, 1939)
claims.evidenceLocation: Chapter 4: James Watt and the Separate Condenser, pp. 66-72
claims.truthCondition: Main cylinder is continuously kept at boiling point (~100°C) with a steam jacket, while the condenser vessel remains cold (~30°C)
claims.simplificationBoundaries: Trace heat conduction occurs through the exhaust valve duct, minimized by intermittent valve timing
claims.predictiveQuestion: Why did Newcomen's engine consume four times more coal than Watt's engine?
claims.predictedAnswer: Newcomen repeatedly chilled the massive cylinder walls with cold water spray, wasting huge fuel energy reheating them on every stroke

claims.statement: Cutting off live steam early in the stroke allows expansive working where internal energy of steam performs mechanical work along an adiabatic curve.
claims.verifiableSource: Carnot S. (Reflections on the Motive Power of Fire, 1824) / P-V Indicator History
claims.evidenceLocation: Watt-Southern Indicator Diagram Archives, Science Museum London
claims.truthCondition: Net work output equals the closed line integral W = ∮ P dV representing the enclosed area of the 4-phase cycle
claims.simplificationBoundaries: Actual expansion is polytropic (P V^n = const with n ≈ 1.13) rather than ideal adiabatic due to minor heat transfer
claims.predictiveQuestion: What thermodynamic parameter determines the work done per cycle?
claims.predictedAnswer: The enclosed cyclic integral area ∮ P dV on the Pressure-Volume diagram

claims.statement: Watt's three-bar parallel motion linkage constrains the piston rod point to an approximately straight vertical line, eliminating lateral cylinder wear.
claims.verifiableSource: Ferguson E. (Kinematics of Mechanisms from the Time of Watt, Smithsonian Institution, 1962)
claims.truthCondition: Inflection point on coupler link traces a lemniscate of Watt whose central segment deviates less than 0.1mm from a true vertical line over the design stroke
claims.simplificationBoundaries: Linkage members maintain rigid invariant lengths while beam rotates through ±14 degrees
claims.predictiveQuestion: Why was the parallel motion linkage essential for double-acting steam engines?
claims.predictedAnswer: Piston rods in double-acting engines must push upward as well as pull downward, requiring rigid vertical guidance without buckling or lateral bore wear
